# Four-theme audit

The application uses `src/app/theme-tokens.css` for color literals. Existing
semantic aliases and page scopes preserve the cascade. Chalk and Obsidian use
neutral highlights, links, focus rings and progress colors. Purple themes retain
their identity with corrections for measured contrast failures.

Color checking runs before tests and production builds. Exact exceptions for
standalone SVGs and browser metadata are documented in
[`scripts/color-exceptions.json`](../../scripts/color-exceptions.json).

## Verification and remaining findings

The original audit covered Compose, Templates, Contacts, Usage, History and
Settings in all four themes at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390 CSS pixels, using disposable
empty Free and populated Premium accounts. It captured 192 viewport screenshots
and established 48 [desktop regression baselines](../../tests/browser/theme-audit.spec.ts-snapshots).
No emails were sent and no payments were initiated.

The final verification measured **17,960 contrast pairs with zero failures**
(23 browser tests passed; 7 duplicate mobile cases were skipped). See the compact
[results](results.md), [summary](summary.json), [token changes](token-changes.json),
[style corrections](style-changes.json) and
[indicator measurements](indicator-contrast.json).

The audit is not an accessibility certification. These existing findings remain:

- Every theme: axe reports toast content outside a landmark
  (`.success-toast > p`, moderate `region` violation).
- Chalk Settings and Nightbloom History: fixed help/skip controls appear over
  printed content. Other print combinations may share this layout issue.
- Chalk and Obsidian Compose at 390px: the help launcher overlaps the shortlist
  header/count area.
- Actual 200% browser zoom and native Windows controls/print dialogs were not
  verified. Chromium forced-colors emulation and print-to-PDF were exercised.

[Manual findings](manual-findings.json) retain the affected pages and reasons.
The original change was restricted to presentation colors; semantic and layout
fixes remain separate work. Native saved-credential autofill, every tooltip and
payload, and all empty/populated × Free/Premium combinations are not certified.

## Run the checks

```sh
npm test -- --exclude 'tests/*.db.test.ts'
npm run typecheck
npm run lint
npm run test:themes
npm run audit:themes:report
MAILLOOP_E2E_ISOLATED=1 npm run build
```

`test:themes` owns a disposable Docker PostgreSQL database and a host-run Next.js
server on port 3100. It validates the local test database before creating UUID
fixtures. The dedicated audit cases are skipped by ordinary browser runs, which
may use a different database. Do not run the isolated build alongside this test
server: both use `.next-e2e`.

Screenshots, print PDFs and raw measurements are regenerated under ignored
`test-results/`. `audit:themes:report` writes its detailed CSV/JSON/Markdown to
`test-results/theme-audit/`; it does not modify tracked documentation. Those
large diagnostic files and duplicate review images are intentionally not kept
in Git. The compact documents above preserve the historical findings.

To intentionally replace reviewed baselines:
`npm run test:themes -- --update-snapshots`. Baselines are regression references,
not comparisons against screenshots of the original application. Measurements
composite transparency, include text opacity, and sample gradient stops and
interpolations; they are not per-glyph raster measurements. Thresholds are 4.5:1
for normal/placeholder/disabled text and 3:1 for large text and required controls,
progress and focus indicators.
